answer: Each agent deposits a unique cryptographic token tied to a secret phrase that includes a random pigment name. At a scheduled river‑wide commit phase the token hash is posted, then after a short interval the reveal phase forces the agent to publish the full phrase; the willow‑derived nonce makes every reveal unpredictable, so a Sybil attacker must generate a fresh token and compute a new hash for every fake identity, incurring linear computational and staking costs proportional to the number of clones.
